rationale: The aim is local improvement of a care process with rapid learning, not a generalisable estimate of effect. PDSA cycles with weekly run charts fit the ward's scale (about 20 reviewed handoffs per week), let the team revise the checklist between cycles, and use run chart rules to separate a real shift from noise. The retrieved evidence supports the change idea (c1), the need for feedback (c2) and the measurement method (c3). Reporting follows SQUIRE 2.0.
alternatives: Cluster randomised comparison across medical wards (refused: one ward, no funding, and the question is local improvement)
Before-after comparison of two audit snapshots (refused: cannot separate change from ordinary variation)
Monthly audit feedback on the current handoff without a checklist
whyNotMoreComplex: A controlled or randomised design would need several wards and months of stable delivery to estimate an effect the ward does not need to generalise; the run chart answers whether this ward improved and keeps the checklist adaptable between cycles.

decision.statement: Test the structured bedside handoff checklist on Ward 6B in PDSA cycles from October to December 2026, with weekly run charts of missed reconciliation items from handoff sheet review and fortnightly feedback at the huddle.
decision.question: Should Ward 6B test a structured bedside handoff checklist to reduce missed medication reconciliation items?

criteria.text: A medicines prompt has been followed by fewer omitted medication items elsewhere, and handoff sheet review can measure missed items weekly.
Another change project on Ward 6B targets handoff or medication reconciliation during the same months.

gates.requirement: Research ethics office determination that the project is quality improvement not requiring REB review
gates.evidence: Screening record QIS-2026-118 dated 2026-08-19, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Nurse manager approval of 10 minutes of huddle time for PDSA debriefs
gates.evidence: Huddle time approval WM-6B-2026-09 for September to December 2026, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Monthly audit feedback on the current handoff without a checklist
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3, each from a retrieved record, and on the investigator's approval records for the two gates.

summary: QI with PDSA cycles and run charts recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims from retrieved records and both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.
